# Detailed solution - grsim-04-07

The output pair $M_1$–$M_2$ is a cascode whose gate bias is generated by $M_3$–$M_6$. Making $M_4$ weaker than the others raises the bias on $M_2$'s gate just enough to keep $M_1$ at $V_{DS1}=V_{ov}$, so the output can go down to $2V_{ov}$. Constraint (i) then fixes $V_{ov}$, constraint (iii) fixes the minimum channel length through $R_o\approx g_mr_o^2$, and constraint (ii) fixes $W/L$. A short area argument shows that this choice minimizes the gate area.

### Step 1 — Bias voltages generated by $M_3$–$M_6$

All devices carry $I=50\ \mu$A. $M_3$ is diode-connected, so $V_{GS3}=V_t+V_{ov}$. With $(W/L)_4=\tfrac14(W/L)$, the same current needs twice the overdrive in $M_4$: $V_{GS4}=V_t+2V_{ov}$. The gate of $M_5$ (= gate of $M_4$) is therefore at

$$
V_{G5}=V_{GS3}+V_{GS4}=2V_t+3V_{ov}.
$$

$M_5$ is a source follower biased by $M_6$ (a mirror of $M_3$, also 50 μA), so it drops $V_{GS5}=V_t+V_{ov}$, and the gate of $M_2$ sits at

$$
V_{G2}=2V_t+3V_{ov}-(V_t+V_{ov})=V_t+2V_{ov}.
$$

$M_2$'s source, $M_1$'s drain, is one $V_{GS2}=V_t+V_{ov}$ lower: $V_{DS1}=V_{ov}$, exactly the edge of saturation for $M_1$. $M_2$ stays active while $V_{DS2}\ge V_{ov}$, so

$$
V_{OUT(\min)}=V_{DS1}+V_{ov}=2V_{ov}.
$$

### Step 2 — Overdrive from constraint (i)

$V_{OUT(\min)}=2V_{ov}\le0.2$ V gives $V_{ov}\le0.1$ V. Choose $V_{ov}=0.1$ V; Step 4 shows that the largest allowed overdrive minimizes area. Then

$$
g_m=\frac{2I}{V_{ov}}=\frac{2(50\ \mu\mathrm A)}{0.1\ \mathrm V}=1\ \mathrm{mA/V}.
$$

### Step 3 — Channel length from constraint (iii)

A change of less than 0.02% of 50 μA per volt requires

$$
R_o\ge\frac{1\ \mathrm V}{(0.0002)(50\ \mu\mathrm A)}=100\ \mathrm{M\Omega}.
$$

With $\lambda=(dX_d/dV_{DS})/L_{\mathrm{eff}}$,

$$
r_o=\frac1{\lambda I}=\frac{L_{\mathrm{eff}}}{(0.02\ \mu\mathrm m/\mathrm V)(50\ \mu\mathrm A)}=\left(\frac{L_{\mathrm{eff}}}{1\ \mu\mathrm m}\right)1\ \mathrm{M\Omega}.
$$

The cascode output resistance is $R_o=r_{o2}(1+g_{m2}r_{o1})+r_{o1}=r_o(2+g_mr_o)$. Writing $x=L_{\mathrm{eff}}/(1\ \mu\mathrm m)$, the condition is $x(2+1000x)\ \mathrm{M\Omega}\ge100\ \mathrm{M\Omega}$:

$$
1000x^2+2x-100\ge0\;\Rightarrow\;x\ge0.315,\qquad L_{\mathrm{eff}}\ge0.315\ \mu\mathrm m .
$$

Take $L_{\mathrm{eff}}=0.32\ \mu$m, i.e. $L_{\mathrm{drwn}}=0.32+2(0.09)=0.50\ \mu$m, above the 0.4-μm minimum. Then $r_o=320$ kΩ and $R_o=0.32\ \mathrm{M\Omega}\,(2+320)=103$ MΩ.

### Step 4 — Width from constraint (ii), and why this minimizes area

$$
\frac W{L_{\mathrm{eff}}}=\frac{2I}{k'V_{ov}^2}=\frac{2(50\ \mu\mathrm A)}{(194\ \mu\mathrm{A/V^2})(0.1\ \mathrm V)^2}=51.5,\qquad W=51.5\times0.32\ \mu\mathrm m=16.5\ \mu\mathrm m .
$$

For each device the gate area is $WL=(W/L)L^2\propto L^2/V_{ov}^2$, so the area is smallest with the largest $V_{ov}$ that (i) allows and the shortest $L$ that (iii) allows. Shortening $L$ further would need a larger $g_m$, hence a smaller $V_{ov}$, which costs more area than it saves.

### Step 5 — The design

| Device | $W$ | $L_{\mathrm{drwn}}$ ($L_{\mathrm{eff}}$) | $W/L_{\mathrm{eff}}$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $M_1$, $M_2$, $M_3$, $M_5$, $M_6$ | 16.5 μm | 0.50 μm (0.32 μm) | 51.5 |
| $M_4$ | 4.1 μm | 0.50 μm (0.32 μm) | 12.9 |

Total gate area: $(5\times16.5+4.1)\ \mu\mathrm m\times0.50\ \mu\mathrm m\approx43\ \mu\mathrm m^2$. Because $V_{DS1}=V_{ov}$ puts $M_1$ exactly at the edge of saturation, a practical design would make $M_4$ slightly smaller than one quarter, to give $M_1$ some margin.

### Step 6 — SPICE check

The deck uses the effective length directly with $\lambda=0.02/0.32=0.0625\ \mathrm{V^{-1}}$:

```spice
* grsim-04-07 high-swing cascode mirror design check
VDD  vdd 0 3
IIN  vdd g4 50u
M4   g4 g4 d3 0 nch W=4.125u L=0.32u
M3   d3 d3 0 0 nch W=16.5u L=0.32u
M5   vdd g4 g2 0 nch W=16.5u L=0.32u
M6   g2 d3 0 0 nch W=16.5u L=0.32u
M2   out g2 d1 0 nch W=16.5u L=0.32u
M1   d1 d3 0 0 nch W=16.5u L=0.32u
VOUT out 0 1
.model nch nmos level=1 kp=194u vto=0.6 lambda=0.0625
.control
op
print v(g4) v(d3) v(g2) v(d1)
tf v(d1) VOUT
print all
dc VOUT 0 3 1m
let iout = -i(VOUT)
wrdata iv.txt iout
.endc
.end
```

| Quantity | Design value | ngspice |
|---|---|---|
| $V_{G2}=V_t+2V_{ov}$ | 0.80 V | 0.799 V |
| $V_{DS1}=V_{ov}$ | 0.10 V | 0.103 V |
| $I_{OUT}$ | 50 μA | 48.2 μA |
| $R_o$ at $V_{OUT}=1$ V | ≥ 100 MΩ | 119 MΩ (`.tf`); 117–135 MΩ from slopes |
| $\Delta I_{OUT}$ per volt | < 0.02% | 0.015–0.017% |
| Lowest $V_{OUT}$ with both devices active | 0.2 V | ≈ 0.2 V (current flat to 0.001% from 0.2 V up) |

![ngspice IOUT versus VOUT of the designed cascode mirror from 0 to 3 V, flat from about 0.2 V](/q/grsim-04-07/solution-iv.svg)

All three constraints are met. $I_{OUT}$ is 3.6% below 50 μA because of channel-length modulation: $M_1$ operates at $V_{DS1}=0.10$ V while the reference device $M_3$ has $V_{DS3}=V_{GS3}=0.70$ V, so $I_{OUT}/I_{IN}=(1+0.0625\times0.10)/(1+0.0625\times0.70)=0.964$. If 50 μA is required exactly, $I_{IN}$ can be raised to about 51.9 μA. The curve is flat from about 0.2 V upward and falls steeply below it, as both output devices enter triode.
